sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: IP formation assay in HEK 293 cells: Buserelin-stimulated inositol phosphate formation by FLAG-hGnRH-RI was similar to untagged hGnRH-RI, confirming the FLAG epitope does not alter signaling potential.
sites.rationale: GNRHR (UniProt P30968) has no annotated signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1-38 as extracellular, making the N-terminus the sole extracellular terminus available for a tag. L5 reports FLAG-hGnRH-RI with equivalent IP signaling to untagged receptor in HEK 293 cells, providing direct human-protein evidence with functional validation. No specific residue is named in L3/L4/L5, so the junction is topology-derived as a prepend (insert_after_residue=0, before M1). The tag is >36 residues from TM1 (boundary at 39), well clear of any TM constraint. FLAG epitope tag fused to the amino terminus of full-length hGnRH-RI (open-reading frame only) expressed in HEK 293 cells; the construct was validated by comparing its signaling capacity to untagged hGnRH-RI.

sources.claim: Our data revealed that Buserelin, a metabolically stable GnRH agonist, stimulated similar levels of inositol phosphate (IP) formation by both FLAG-hGnRH-RI- and hGnRH-RI cDNA-expressing HEK 293 cells ( Fig. 1A ) suggesting that the FLAG epitope does not alter the signaling potential of the receptor.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression detected by immunological detection in the GPCR library screen; functional assays for GnRHR specifically NOT MEASURED in this study.
sites.rationale: L16 explicitly states the HA tag was inserted 'between the first 5' start codon and the second codon' for class A GPCRs including GnRHR, pinning the junction to after M1 (insert_after_residue=1, residue_before=M, residue_after=A as read from the canonical sequence). This is a named-residue validated position distinct from the prepend (site 1). The junction is 38 residues from TM1 (boundary at 39), well within the extracellular N-terminal domain (1-38). Python confirmed seq[0]='M' and seq[1]='A'. For class A GPCRs (including GnRHR) lacking an extended N-terminal domain, an HA-coding sequence was inserted between the first start codon and the second codon in a GPCR library to enable immunological detection of surface-expressed receptors.

sources.claim: For GPCRs lacking an extended N-terminal domain (i.e., class A and olfactory receptors), we inserted an influenza hemagglutinin (HA)-coding sequence between the first 5ʹ start codon and the second codon in order to facilitate universal immunological detection.

literature_notes: GNRHR (P30968, 328 aa) is a GPCR with no annotated signal peptide; the N-terminal 38 residues are extracellular per the topology landmarks. All ledger lines converge on the extracellular N-terminus as the only published tag-insertion site. Two distinct junctions are supported: (1) a prepend before M1 (insert_after_residue=0), grounded in L3/L4/L5 (FLAG-hGnRHR with function validation) and corroborated by L1/L2 (NanoLuc-hGnRHR, surface confirmed), L6/L7/L9/L10 (HA-hGnRHR, surface confirmed), and indirect ortholog evidence in L11 (rat HA-GnRHR), L12/L13 (mouse HA-GnRHR), L14 (pig/fish FLAG-GnRHR); (2) after M1 (insert_after_residue=1), explicitly named in L16 for class A GPCRs including GnRHR. No ledger line supports an insertion in ECL1 (98-115), ECL2 (185-212), or ECL3 (301-306) as a tag site. The K191Δ deletion mentioned in L1/L2 is a receptor modification to improve surface trafficking, not a tag insertion site, and is not placed in other_positions as it does not fit 'intracellular' or 'abrogates_function' categories (it is a deletion that improves expression). The NanoLuc construct in L1/L2 uses an IL6 secretory signal peptide fused to NanoLuc itself (not to hGnRHR), so the hGnRHR N-terminus remains the tag-attachment point; however, the K191Δ co-modification confounds independent function assessment of the N-terminal tag alone, so this line is used as corroborating evidence for site 1 rather than primary.
